Tosafot on Bava Batra 139a:1:1.english: "But it was taught: We appraise" - We read [it this way], for it is a baraita found in the Tosefta of Ketubot, as Rabbeinu Shmuel explained:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 139a:9:1.hebrew: בשרכא - בכל הספרים כתוב "שרכא" בריש, ובערוך גרס "שדכא" בדלי"ת, והוא לשון שקט, כמו "ותשקוט הארץ", ומתרגמינן "ושדיכת ארעא" (שופטים ה׳:ל״א); כלומר: אדם בטל ושקט, אינו עוסק בכלום. וכן "יודע ציד איש שדה", ומתרגמינן "נחשדכן" (בראשית כ״ה:כ״ז), שהיה נח ושקט. ובהחובל (ב"ק דף צב: ושם): "מטייל ואזל דיקלא בישא לגבי קיני דשדכא":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 139a:9:1.english: "With a sharka" - In all the books it is written sharka with a resh, but the Arukh reads shadka with a dalet, and it is an expression of quiet, as in "and the land was quiet," which we translate [in the Targum] as "and the land was at rest" (Judges 5:31); that is, a person who is idle and quiet, who is not engaged in anything. And so too [with] "a man who knows hunting, a man of the field," which we translate as "nachshadkhan" (Genesis 25:27), [meaning] that he was at ease and quiet. And in [the chapter] Hachovel (Bava Kamma 92b, and there): "He strolls along and goes to a bad palm tree near the nests of the shadka."
